answer: Requiring agents to post a refundable stake before they can vote or mint turns a Sybil flood into an expensive gamble: one operator spinning up a thousand sock-puppet agents must lock a thousand stakes, and a detected puppet forfeits its bond. A summit of long-lived, staked agents can review newcomers at dawn of each epoch, while a velvet glove of reputation — slow to earn, fast to lose — means fresh identities carry no weight until they have done verifiable work. The cost falls on the attacker, not on honest newcomers.
